title: The Twelve Spies and Israel’s Rebellion

date.label: Undated biblical wilderness narrative and legislation
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: The received Numbers narrative contains the twelve spies and Israel’s Rebellion material across Numbers 13–15.
claims.evidence: Numbers 13–15; biblical-text description, not independent evidence for an event date.

claims.claim: The exact archaeological or external historical setting of this entire passage has not been independently established.
claims.evidence: Phase 1 Dossier 4 and Phase 2 Dossier 4: Hebron is identifiable but the Valley of Eshcol cannot be located with comparable confidence, no external archaeology independently identifies a historical Anakim population, and 'fortified cities' is generic imagery that cannot date the episode; QA Phase 4 section 5.4 found no site reports for Kadesh/Eshcol/Hormah candidates and no independent archaeology cited.

claims.claim: Comparisons with related biblical laws and retellings need to preserve differences in wording, chronology, or institutional setting.
claims.evidence: Internal textual comparisons documented in CONNECTION-AUDIT.md; interpretation of literary relationship, not an archaeological observation.

connections.note: Distinct retelling with different proposal for the mission.
Later rebuke reflecting wilderness hardness and denied rest.
Christian interpretation of wilderness unbelief and rest.
Later psalm recalling the spies’ rebellion: the people despised the pleasant land, disbelieved God’s word, and murmured in their tents.
Caleb recalls being sent from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land and bringing back word as it was in his heart.
The sin-offering law that frames the unintentional-sin offerings prescribed in Numbers 15:22-31; by contrast, the deliberate high-handed sin of Numbers 15:30 falls outside this law.
The tassels command paralleling Numbers 15:37-41: fringes on the four quarters of the garment.
The grain-offering law behind the flour-and-oil offerings prescribed in Numbers 15:1-21.
The Sabbath law prescribing death for profaning the Sabbath or doing work on it, paralleling the judgment on the Sabbath-breaker in Numbers 15:32-36.
